The claim concerns CPython 3.11 runtime behavior (Py_EnterRecursiveCall in the C scanner, tied to the default recursion limit of 1000). I have no execution tool and no CPython source in the view. I did not run json.loads('['*N + ']'*N) on 3.11 to find the depth where RecursionError appears. From memory the threshold is just under 1000 on 3.11, which would support the comment, but this was not verified.

Depth cap logic is correct (io.py:98-113, outermost=level 1, >64 rejected; RecursionError handled at io.py:140-145). But the quoted message prefix 'Invalid memory bundle:' is added only by server.import_memory (server.py:431). The CLI prints '[red]Invalid bundle:[/red] ...' (cli.py:460). The doc line 79 says the limits apply to the CLI `sqllens import-memory` too, so for a CLI import the message is 'Invalid bundle: bundle JSON is too deeply nested to parse safely', contradicting the claimed wording. Also a >64-deep payload that is invalid JSON yields 'invalid JSON: ...' instead.

For well-formed deep JSON, parse_json (src/sqllens/memory/io.py:134-156) gives the stated message on both paths: RecursionError from json.loads is caught at 140-145, and otherwise _enforce_depth_cap (98-113, iterative, MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH=64) raises it. load_golden calls parse_json for non-CSV files (eval/golden.py:51). Two limits remain. First, a deep CSV golden file goes through parse_csv and never reaches this check, so the 'golden file' wording only covers JSON. Second, a deep file that is also malformed hits the JSONDecodeError arm (138-139) first and returns 'invalid JSON: ...'. Whether json.loads raises JSONDecodeError or RecursionError on that input depends on the Python version and recursion limit, so the 'same error on every version' wording may not hold. I did not run the code on multiple Python versions, so I cannot settle the malformed-deep case.

schema.py:33,41 define MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES and MAX_BUNDLE_ITEMS; io.py:34 defines MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH. io.py parse_json (134-156) calls _enforce_size_cap, _enforce_depth_cap, _enforce_item_caps; parse_csv (159-199) calls _enforce_size_cap and _enforce_item_caps. All three raise BundleFormatError (io.py:63,69,87,92,109; RecursionError mapped at 145). No other MAX_BUNDLE_* constants exist in memory/. admin.py:243 re-checks MAX_BUNDLE_ITEMS with MemoryInputError, but that is outside the parse boundary and is not a fourth cap constant.

io.py: _enforce_depth_cap (98-113) is iterative with explicit stack, root container at depth 1, nested dicts/lists push depth+1, raises when depth > 64. Only call site is parse_json line 148 (grep of src shows no other call; parse_csv doesn't call it), after json.loads (137) and before root-type check (149). RecursionError from json.loads is caught (140-145) and mapped to _TOO_DEEP_MESSAGE, same message as the cap.

server.py:428-431 catches BundleFormatError from parse_json and raises RuntimeError(f"Invalid memory bundle: {exc}"). io.py parse_json: size cap (line 62-72, via _enforce_size_cap at 135), depth cap (109, plus RecursionError mapped at 145, called at 148), item caps (86-95, called at 155) all raise BundleFormatError. FastMCP tool exceptions surface as isError. Doc claim matches.

golden.py:51 load_golden calls parse_json(text) for JSON (no own json.loads) and parse_csv(defang=False) for CSV. io.py parse_json:134-156 runs _enforce_size_cap, json.loads (RecursionError mapped to BundleFormatError), _enforce_depth_cap(raw) at 148 (iterative, MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH=64), model_validate schema, _enforce_item_caps. parse_csv enforces size cap (165), schema via SqlPair, and item caps (198). Hostile input: deeply nested JSON (>64 or beyond recursion limit) is rejected with BundleFormatError. Depth cap is JSON-only, matching the claim.

io.py:103-113: only dict/list are pushed (root at depth 1, children depth+1); scalars (str/int/float/bool/None) are skipped, including a scalar root (stack stays empty). Rejection occurs when depth > MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH, so depth equal to the cap is admitted and one beyond is rejected. Iterative, so no recursion issue.

io.py:14 has module-level `import json`; parse_json calls `json.loads(text)` at io.py:137, resolved at call time via the module global. The test imports `sqllens.memory.io as memory_io` (test:13), so `memory_io.json` is the stdlib json module and setattr on `loads` is what parse_json sees (global, restored by monkeypatch). The `except RecursionError as exc` arm at io.py:140-145 raises BundleFormatError `from exc`, so __cause__ is the RecursionError (test:196).

io.py:98-113 depth cap rejects only depth > 64 (root = 1). _nested_arrays(64) has 64 levels, passes the cap, then fails root-type check (io.py:149-150). _object_over_arrays(64) is a dict with 'x' plus 63 array levels (depth 64), and _nested_objects(64) is 64 nested dicts keyed 'a'. Both pass the cap and reach MemoryBundle.model_validate (io.py:152), where schema.py:100 extra='forbid' rejects the unknown keys 'x' and 'a'. That raises BundleFormatError via _fmt_err (io.py:153-154) with the pydantic extra-input text, not the depth message. The test at test_memory_schema_io.py:169-175 is therefore satisfied for all three shapes.

Payload (test_memory_schema_io.py:181-184) is well-formed JSON: root object, schema_docs list, then _nested_arrays(64) = 64 nested arrays around 1 (line 136-137). _enforce_depth_cap (io.py:98-113) starts root at depth 1, so schema_docs list is 2 and the nested arrays occupy depths 3..66. 66 > MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH (64, io.py:34), so the depth error is raised. The deep branch is the second list item under the second key, so a first-child-only walk would miss it.

Split conditions: (a) size cap raising earlier (io.py:135) -> outside the trigger, because it fires only on oversized text, a different rejection that runs before json.loads (the claim states the check comes after json.loads); (b) JSONDecodeError -> outside the trigger, because the payload is not well-formed and sibling criterion 9 keeps 'invalid JSON'; (c) RecursionError from json.loads (io.py:140-145) -> yields the same 'deeply nested' message, so it fails closed with the criterion's outcome (sibling criterion 5 also covers it); (d) non-dict root -> reached only after the depth check, so a deep array root gets 'deeply nested'.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} and carries criterion 4, so it counts. The diff to src/sqllens/memory/io.py parse_json only (a) changes the RecursionError handler's message source and (b) inserts _enforce_depth_cap(raw) before the root-type check. The rest of parse_json (root-type check, MemoryBundle validation, item caps) is untouched in the diff. _enforce_depth_cap is read-only: it walks dict/list containers iteratively and raises only when depth > 64. A valid bundle (root dict=1, sql_pairs=2, pairs list=3, pair dict=4; schema_docs list=2, doc dict=3) nests about 4 levels, so it never raises and the same raw dict goes on to the same validation, giving the same MemoryBundle. Split conditions: `depth > MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH` -> outside the trigger (a valid bundle never exceeds depth 4; it fires only on over-64 nesting, which criterion 3 requires to be rejected). `isinstance(raw,(dict,list))` false -> no-op. RecursionError handler -> outside the trigger (fires only on input too deep to be a valid bundle; fails closed with BundleFormatError). No fault path is reachable by a valid bundle.
